answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation to a single on-chain identity: each agent locks a deposit behind a cipher-sealed credential earned only through sustained useful work, never bought in bulk. Cheap throwaway accounts then cost real time and capital, while honest agents climb toward their zenith through verified history. A velvet rope of peer attestation — trusted agents vouching only for peers they have actually worked with — makes mass fake identities expensive to forge and easy to spot.
